CALM: Conformer Audio-Language Model

A music genre classifier that listens to 5 seconds of audio and also reads what is known about the track, with both halves frozen and a small fusion layer learning how to combine them.

Accuracy, FMA-Medium, 16 genresRepo README, results table

Code and results on GitHub

The problem

Pre-trained audio encoders already know a lot about music, but fine-tuning one end to end for genre is expensive. I wanted to know how far a cheap fusion layer could go if I froze two large models and trained only the glue between them.

The audio side is the Conformer inside Gemma 4. The text side is Gemma 4's text backbone reading the track title, the artist name and the artist bio from the FMA metadata. Artist tags are left out by default because they leak the genre label. The repo also benchmarks other pre-trained audio encoders on the same split, zero-shot and fine-tuned, so CALM has something real to beat.

How it works

  1. Cut a 5 second clip.Resampled to 16 kHz and turned into mel features by Gemma's feature extractor.
  2. Run the frozen audio tower.The 305M-parameter Conformer returns one 1536-wide vector per audio token.
  3. Embed the track text once.Title, artist and bio go through the frozen text backbone and come out as a single 1536-wide vector.
  4. Project, then cross-attend.Both sides shrink to 512 wide. Two layers of 8-head attention let audio tokens read the text vector and the text vector read the audio.
  5. Pool and classify.Average the audio tokens, join them with the text vector, and a small MLP picks one of 16 genres. Only steps 4 and 5 train.

Limits and next steps

  • The text half sees the artist's bio, which can say a lot about genre. The 83.9% is a result for audio plus metadata, so it is not directly comparable with the audio-only encoders.
  • Each model has one accuracy number. There are no error bars, and FMA-Medium is class-imbalanced, so accuracy hides how it does on small genres. Per-genre F1 is in the repo logs and I have not summarised it here.
  • The repo holds a 153-track Bollywood set meant as an out-of-distribution test. I have not reported results on it.
  • A separate branch adds an interpretability study of how CALM weighs audio against text. It is still being worked on, so none of its numbers are on this page.
